rounds.text: Rane (Madras) Ltd is currently experiencing a powerful fundamental disconnect where profit growth is significantly outpacing share price appreciation [E57]. While the stock has delivered a 30% compounded profit growth over the last five years [E19], the most recent trailing twelve-month profit growth has surged to an impressive 188% [E21]. This operational momentum is backed by high-quality cash generation, evidenced by a 2.05x cash conversion ratio that ensures reported profits are fully supported by actual cash flow [E34]. Furthermore, the company is actively investing in its future, as shown by a 30.1% increase in capital work in progress [E41], while simultaneously reducing total borrowings from Rs 813 Cr to Rs 752 Cr [E40]. The market appears to be under-appreciating this trajectory, as the current price implies only 12% earnings growth despite the company’s demonstrated ability to exceed 18% in its base case [E48]. Conceded: the company faces a tight liquidity position with a current ratio of 0.92x [E39], and promoter holdings have declined by 2.20 percentage points since September 2023 [E42].

Rane (Madras) Ltd exhibits concerning liquidity constraints, as evidenced by a current ratio of 0.92x, indicating that current liabilities exceed current assets [E39]. This financial tightness is compounded by a high price-to-book valuation of 4.17x to 4.28x, which sits significantly above the sector benchmark of 2.88x [E2, E7, E62]. Furthermore, the company’s operational efficiency lags behind its peers, with an ROA of 4.72% compared to the sector benchmark of 5.98% [E8]. Investors should also note the ongoing reduction in promoter holdings, which have declined from 72.65% to 70.45% since September 2023 [E42]. While the company has shown strong recent profit growth, the screening engine explicitly flags that earnings growth is now decelerating [E69]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated strong compounded sales and profit growth over the last five years [E15, E19, E60].

The bear’s focus on the current ratio of 0.92x [E39] ignores the company’s robust cash-generating ability, where operating cash flow of Rs 219 Cr fully covers profits with a 2.05x conversion ratio [E34, E35]. While the P/B ratio is higher than the sector benchmark [E7], this premium is justified by superior profitability, as the company’s ROE of 14.32% and ROCE of 13.6% consistently outperform sector benchmarks of 11.49% and 12.54% respectively [E9, E10]. Conceded: the ROA of 4.72% is lower than the sector benchmark of 5.98% [E8]. Regarding promoter holdings, the slight reduction [E42] is countered by the fact that institutional interest is rising, with both foreign and domestic holdings increasing since 2023 [E43, E44]. Furthermore, the claim of decelerating earnings growth [E69] is contradicted by the most recent trailing twelve-month profit growth of 188% [E21], which significantly outpaces long-term averages [E18, E19]. Finally, the company is actively strengthening its balance sheet by reducing total borrowings from Rs 813 Cr to Rs 752 Cr [E40].
